content.title: 2026 WNBA Draft results: Wings take Azzi Fudd No. 1, UCLA sets record
content.text: Azzi Fudd of UConn poses with WNBA Commissioner Cathy Engelbert after being selected with the 1st pick in the first round by the Dallas Wings during the 2026 WNBA Draft at The Shed on April 13, 2026 in New York City.Angelina Katsanis/Getty Images WNBA Draft recap: Azzi Fudd goes No. 1 to Dallas Wings, UCLA smashes record, Flau'jae Johnson traded to Seattle Storm Top 5 picks: Dallas Wings take Azzi Fudd at No. 1; Minnesota Lynx draft Olivia Miles No. 2; Seattle Storm take Awa Fam Thiam at No. 3; Washington Mystics pick Lauren Betts at No. 4; Chicago Sky take Gabriela Jaquez at No. 5. UConn connection: With the Wings, Fudd will reunite with Paige Bueckers, the reigning WNBA Rookie of the Year. Bueckers and Fudd helped lead UConn to the 2025 national championship. Flau’jae Johnson traded: After the Golden State Valkyries took the LSU star with the No. 8 pick, they traded Johnson to the Seattle Storm. UCLA women’s basketball sets record: Six Bruins were selected in Monday’s draft. That breaks an overall WNBA Draft record for most players taken from one school, which was four. WNBA rookie salary: With salaries on the rise in the WNBA, Fudd’s 4-year deal with the Wings will pay her $2,238,360 spread across four years. Expansion teams make 1st picks: The Toronto Tempo took Kiki Rice at No. 6 and the Portland Fire drafted Iyana Martin Carrion at No. 7. Full WNBA Draft results. The night’s first round is over.Article continues below this ad Connecticut Sun take Gianna Kneepkens at No. 15 8:26 p.m.: UCLA gets its fifth player taken tonight, a record for a WNBA draft.Gianna Kneepkens is the final pick of the first round.Article continues below this ad Seattle Storm take Taina Mair at No. 14 8:24 p.m.: Duke guard Taina Mair is the Storm's second pick of the first round.A 5-foot-9 guard, Mair was a first-team All-ACC player this past season. Atlanta Dream takes Madina Okot 8:20 p.m.: With the No. 13 pick, the Dream take South Carolina center Madina Okot.Article continues below this adA 6-foot-6 post, Okot averaged a double-double this past season. Connecticut Sun use No. 12 pick on Nell Angloma 8:15 p.m.: France's Nell Angloma is the selection for the Sun.Angloma is a 5-foot-11 forward and known as a solid scoring option.Article continues below this adThe Sun franchise is long for Connecticut. The team is slated to move to Houston after this season. Washington Mystics take Cotie McMahon 8:07 p.m.: With the No. 11 pick, the Mystics take Ole Miss star Cotie McMahon.A 6-foot forward, McMahon started her college career at Ohio State.Article continues below this ad Indiana Fever drafts Raven Johnson to join Caitlin Clark, Aliyah Boston 8:03 p.m.: At No. 10, the Indiana Fever select Raven Johnson.A point guard, Johnson starred for Dawn Staley at South Carolina. Washington Mystics take Angela Dugalic at No. 9 7:59 p.m.: The Mystics take the fourth UCLA player of the night at No. 9.Article continues below this adThat's Angela Dugalic, a 6-foot-4 forward Washington pairs with 6-foot-7 Lauren Betts, who the Mystics took at No. 4. Golden State Valkyries take Flau’jae Johnson 7:51 p.m.: LSU great Flau'jae Johnson is the No. 8 pick.Golden State opts for the high-scoring guard who starred for Kim Mulkey.Article continues below this ad Portland Fire takes Iyana Martin Carrion at No. 7 7:48 p.m.: Portland goes for a bit of a surprise at No. 7 with Iyana Martin Carrion, a 5-foot-9 guard from Spain. Toronto Tempo use 1st-ever pick on Kiki Rice 7:43 p.m.: One of the WNBA's two new expansion teams, Portland uses the No. 6 overall pick on Kiki Rice.Article continues below this adThat's three consecutive players from UCLA taken in this year's draft. Chicago Sky use No. 5 pick on Gabriela Jaquez 7:36 p.m.: Back-to-back picks of UCLA Bruins.Jaquez was a late-riser in the draft after helping lead UCLA to the national championship.Article continues below this adShe is the younger sister of NBA player Jaime Jaquez. Washington Mystics select Lauren Betts 7:31 p.m.: Washington goes big, and adds 6-foot-7 Lauren Betts to its roster with the No. 4 pick.Betts, an All-American, is coming off leading UCLA to the national title.Article continues below this ad Seattle Storm select Awa Fam Thiam 7:26 p.m.: From Spain, Awa Fam Thiam is the pick for the Storm.A 6-foot-6 big, Fam Thiam can play either the 4 or 5. She did not play in college, but has played professionally since 2021 despite only being 19 years old. Minnesota Lynx select Olivia Miles 7:18 p.m.: With the No. 2 pick, Minnesota adds TCU guard Olivia Miles.Article continues below this adMiles averaged 19.6 points, 7.2 rebounds and 6.6 assists per game this past season.The versatile guard started her college career at Notre Dame. Dallas Wings take Azzi Fudd at No. 1 7:12 p.m.: With the No. 1 pick in this year’s draft, the Dallas Wings reunite UConn legends Azzi Fudd and Paige Bueckers.Article continues below this adThe Wings selected Fudd, a 5-foot-11 guard with a great outside shot, over Lauren Betts, Awa Fam Thiam and Olivia Miles.Bueckers is the reigning Rookie of the Year. Azzi Fudd appears likely to head to Dallas 7:02 p.m.: As the WNBA Draft gets underway, a consensus is forming that UConn great Azzi Fudd will join Paige Bueckers in Dallas.Article continues below this adThe Wings own the No. 1 pick, and GM Curt Miller is on the clock. Who goes No. 1? Does UCLA dominate? 6:50 p.m.: This year’s WNBA Draft starts up in a matter of minutes.There are plenty of storylines to follow.Article continues below this ad There is a four-way race atop the draft to be the No. 1 pick for the Dallas Wings. Lauren Betts, Awa Fam Thiam, Olivia Miles and Azzi Fudd are all in the mix. UCLA could break the record for most players picked in a single draft. That record is five, and UCLA is expected to have six players picked tonight. Who joins Caitlin Clark on the Fever? Indiana picks No. 10 tonight in the first round. Azzi Fudd is one of the top prospects for tonight’s WNBA Draft.C. Morgan Engel/NCAA Photos via Getty Images Azzi Fudd joins ESPN broadcast as rumors swirl she’ll go No. 1 UConn star Azzi Fudd has momentum as the projected No. 1 pick in tonight’s WNBA Draft.Article continues below this adOn ESPN’s pre-draft show, she was asked about that status and said: “I’m just so grateful to be here. This whole weekend has been such a pinch-me experience. It’s been so surreal.” How did the Dallas Wings get the No. 1 pick? The Wings received the No. 1 pick in the 2026 WNBA Draft after winning the draft lottery this past November.Dallas, which also had the No. 1 pick last year, entered the draft lottery with a 42% chance to get the top pick after going 10-34 last season.Article continues below this adThe Wings’ 2024 No. 1 pick was UConn great Paige Bueckers, who won WNBA Rookie of the Year.The full first round’s order goes like this … Dallas Minnesota Seattle Washington Chicago Toronto Portland Golden State Washington Indiana Washington Connecticut Atlanta Seattle Connecticut What channel was the WNBA Draft on Monday? ESPN is your home for broadcast coverage of tonight’s draft.Article continues below this adTonight’s 7 p.m. draft is also able to be streamed on ESPN Unlimited or Fubo.Ryan Ruocco, Rebecca Lobo, Andraya Carter and Holly Rowe will lead the broadcast. Who does Curt Miller take at No. 1 for the Dallas Wings? This year’s WNBA Draft is a rare one in major U.S. professional sports in that the No. 1 pick is truly up for grabs.Article continues below this adDallas Wings general manager Curt Miller, a former coach in the W, has a number of choices to pick from at No. 1 and needs to take advantage of the opportunity to pair reigning Rookie of the Year Paige Bueckers with another star.The question for Miller and the Wings: How to best build around Bueckers? If the answer is a pure big, that’s UCLA star Lauren Betts. A shooter? That means UConn’s Azzi Fudd will head to Dallas. If Dallas wants another playmaker, TCU’s Olivia Miles will be the pick. Or, if the Wings value taking the player with the highest ceiling, Spain’s Awa Fam Thiam could be the choice. Which team lands Flau’jae Johnson? After starring at LSU for coach Kim Mulkey, Flau’jae Johnson is one of the most-recognizable names in this year’s WNBA Draft.Article continues below this adDuring her college career, Johnson helped the Tigers win a national championship, scored a bunch of points — oh, and further developed her blossoming hip-hop career.This past season, the 5-foot-10 guard averaged 14.6 points per game. The 22-year-old is likely to be selected within tonight’s top 10. Olivia Miles goes from Notre Dame to TCU to … No. 1 pick? Maybe. We’ll find out soon.Article continues below this adNo longer sharing a backcourt with Hannah Hidalgo, Olivia Miles blossomed this past season for TCU. A versatile player, Miles averaged 19.6 points, 7.2 rebounds and 6.6 assists per game, and collected five triple-doubles in leading her team to a spot in the Elite Eight.A 5–foot-10 guard, Miles made 48.1% of her shots this past season, including 35.1% from 3-point territory. Could Awa Fam Thiam be the next WNBA superstar? Awa Fam Thiam is one of the most intriguing prospects in this year’s WNBA Draft, and could go as high as No. 1 to the Dallas Wings. A 6-foot-6 big, Fam Thiam can play either the 4 or 5, and has played professionally since 2021 despite – still – only being 19 years old.Article continues below this adFam Thiam is from Spain, where her parents moved to a few decages ago from Senegal.She did not play college basketball. Lauren Betts leads UCLA contingent UCLA won the national championship and tonight’s WNBA Draft should help illustrate just how good Cori Close’s team was this past season.Article continues below this adLauren Betts, the 6-foot-7 center, could go No. 1.Meanwhile, teammates Angela Dugalić, Gabriela Jaquez, Gianna Kneepkens and Kiki Rice are among the 15 prospects invited to attend tonight’s draft in person.UCLA beat Texas in the Final Four, then topped South Carolina in the title game earlier this month. Could Azzi Fudd rejoin UConn teammate Paige Bueckers? UConn star Azzi Fudd could go No. 1 tonight, which would mean a reunion of Huskies legends.Article continues below this adThe Dallas Wings, owners of tonight’s No. 1 pick, selected Paige Bueckers last year with the No. 1 pick. Bueckers lived up to the hype in her first year in the WNBA and won Rookie of the Year honors.Fudd played with Bueckers and could form a dynamic backcourt with her for the Wings. In her final season at UConn, Fudd averaged 17.3 points per game and helped lead the Huskies to the Final Four. Salaries for tonight’s WNBA Draft picks When the WNBA and WNBAPA reached a deal this past month on their new collective bargaining agreement, player salaries took a significant jump – and tonight’s draft picks will benefit from that.Article continues below this adSpotrack has a full look at the rookie salary scale, and the total salary value for tonight’s No. 1 pick tonight is $2,238,360 spread across four years.The rookie year salary for the No. 1 pick is $500,000 – a figure that’s larger on its own than 2025 No. 1 pick Paige Buecker’s initial four-year deal of $348,198. Which players will be at tonight’s WNBA Draft? Fifteen players are expected to be at tonight’s draft at The Shed at Hudson Yards in New York City.Article continues below this ad Nell Angloma (France), 5-11 forward Lauren Betts (UCLA/USA), 6-7 center Angela Dugalić (UCLA/USA), 6-4 forward Awa Fam Thiam (Valencia Basket/Spain), 6-4 center Azzi Fudd (Connecticut/USA), 5-11 guard Gabriela Jaquez (UCLA/USA), 6-0 guard Flau’jae Johnson (LSU/USA), 5-10 guard Raven Johnson (South Carolina/USA), 5-9 guard Gianna Kneepkens (UCLA/USA), 6-0 guard Ta’Niya Latson (South Carolina/USA), 5-9 guard Cotie McMahon (Ole Miss/USA), 6-0 forward Olivia Miles (TCU/USA), 5-10 guard Madina Okot (South Carolina/Kenya), 6-6 center Kiki Rice (UCLA/USA), 5-11 guard Marta Suárez (TCU/Spain), 6-3 forward Who has the No. 1 pick? The Dallas Wings, who also had the No. 1 pick in last year’s draft, will select first in this year’s draft. Where and when is the WNBA Draft? The draft takes place tonight at The Shed at Hudson Yards in New York City.Article continues below this ad What time does the 2026 WNBA Draft start? Tonight’s WNBA Draft starts at 7 p.m. When does the WNBA season start? The W’s 30th season starts on May 8, which is a Friday.Article continues below this adThere are three games on opening night, including one of the league’s two new teams in the Toronto Tempo. 7:30 p.m. ET: Connecticut Sun vs. New York Liberty 7:30 p.m. ET: Washington Mystics vs. Toronto Tempo 10 p.m. ET: Golden State Valkyries vs. Seattle Storm On May 9, the defending champion Las Vegas Aces and Caitlin Clark’s Indiana Fever help to continue the opening weekend. 1 p.m. ET: Dallas Wings vs. Indiana Fever 3:30 p.m. ET: Phoenix Mercury vs. Las Vegas Aces 9 p.m. ET: Chicago Sky vs. Portland Fire Article continues below this adHere is the full draft order for the three-round draft.
